name: Glowing reef sentinel
subtitle: coral that signals heat stress early

effects.effect: a jellyfish protein makes any cell that carries its gene glow green
regulator genes switch other genes on and off
the bacteria in the gut steer the body's immunity, weight and mood

effect: a jellyfish protein makes any cell that carries its gene glow green
how: A reef looks fine right up to the week it bleaches, by which point the heat damage is done and nothing can be moved or shaded in time. The algae that live inside coral switch on stress genes days before they are expelled. Seeding a few marked colonies on a reef whose algae carry a glowing protein tied to that stress switch gives a row of sentinels a diver or a moored camera can read, so shading or cooling can start while it still helps.
obstacle: Putting engineered organisms on a wild reef is a decision no country has a process for making.
why: Stress genes are known; releasing engineered symbionts into the sea is the blocker.
real: Coral's own GFP fluorescence drops days before visible bleaching and is used as a non-invasive field indicator, but transgenic Symbiodinium reporters remain irreproducible and transient (1998 GUS work largely unrepeated), so no engineered sentinel colony exists.
